route: code re-derivation from the source question-definition sheet id column (label match), corroborated by raw export headers and self-describing codes; plus route 8-style referent-applicability n ordering as a class-level data check; resp axis from the published DMQ_scales answer-code key
evidence: ROUTE A (label match / exact code re-derivation, primary): the study's DMQs question-definition sheet holds one row per LimeSurvey question with the question code in its own `id` column. Applying the project's published dmqReplacements shortening (Neighbourhood -> Neighbrhd) and then data/peters_2025_covid19_risk_dcts.py's rename (^NrmIn(Ap|Mc)(.+)$ -> group(2).lower()) to the 10 NrmInAp* ids reproduces the live item set exactly: 0 live codes underived, 0 derived codes absent, 10 distinct codes vs 10 live items. The shipped item_text equals that same row's subquestion_en and the shipped resp=1/resp=7 option_text equal its bottom_anchor_bare/top_anchor_bare, 10/10, with resp 2-6 blank 10/10. The chain was independently corroborated at the raw-data end: all 10 NrmInAp* column names are present in the header row of YCR-dataPipeline--sid-100102--rids-1-141.csv (columns 391, 394, 397, 400, 403, 406, 409, 412, 415, 418 of 577). Codes are also self-describing (boss, colleagues, doctor, family, friends, general, government, household, likeme, neighbrhd), so a permutation could not be silent. ROUTE B (data-side corroboration, class-level only): the tool offered '(not applicable)' as answer code 0, which the IRW script drops, so referents that do not apply to every respondent must retain fewest responses. Live per-item n: boss 904, colleagues 1118, then general 1228, household 1238, doctor 1258, friends 1324, family 1342, neighbrhd 1354, likeme 1383, government 1400 -- the two workplace referents are the two smallest, 904 and 1118 against a next-smallest 1228. RESP AXIS: the DMQ_scales sheet states the bi key outright (code 1 = displayed -3, 4 = 0, 7 = +3), so resp=1 -> 'strongly disapprove' and resp=7 -> 'strongly approve' is read off a published key, not inferred. WHAT THIS DOES NOT ESTABLISH: Route A cannot detect an error inside the sheet itself (it is a source-label tie, not a data-side test); Route B separates only the {boss, colleagues} class and does not order items within either class; neither route tests the unlabelled midpoints resp=2..6, which are shipped blank by design, nor any of the non-English administered wordings, which are not shipped.

route: re-run of the processing script over the raw source exports (core model s3), compared cell-by-cell rather than by summary statistic; corroborated by the label match in the study's own question-definition sheet
evidence: Re-derived the IRW long form by hand from two of the study's own raw LimeSurvey exports (https://gitlab.com/a-bc/your-covid-19-risk-data, sid 100110, files rids-1-2583 and rids-2584-5166): melted the 22 PbcCnPr* columns (excluding the 22 amended PbcCnPr*2 columns, which data/peters_2025_covid19_risk_dcts.py does not read), kept resp in 1..5 (code 0 = 'not applicable' dropped), built id as '100110-<orig_id>', and labelled each value with the lower-cased suffix. Merged against irw_fetch() restricted to those ids: 1430 raw cells vs 1430 live cells, 0 cells present on only one side, 0 value disagreements. Per item, n_raw == n_live and mean_raw == mean_live to 3 dp for all 22, e.g. busyplace 82/82 2.439/2.439, techtouch 56/56 4.232/4.232, work 44/44 3.068/3.068, sitclose 52/52 3.038/3.038, sprmrkt 69/69 3.536/3.536. Because every item's response vector is compared individually, any permutation of two item codes would move 44-82 values onto the wrong code and show up as disagreements -- so this distinguishes every item from every other item, not a subscale or a polarity class. Separately, all 22 live item codes reconstruct one-to-one and onto from the DMQs question-definition sheet's own 'id' column (22 sheet rows starting PbcCnPr, 22 live items, 0 either way), and the sheet's scale_type is 'uni' for all 22, which predicts the observed per-item resp range 1..5 22/22. WHAT THIS DOES NOT ESTABLISH: the raw-column -> wording tie is a label match in that sheet (its 'id' column IS the raw LimeSurvey/CSV column name) and is not testable from response data; the unlabelled intermediate options resp 2-4 are not tested and are shipped blank; the endpoint direction (resp 1 = bottom anchor, resp 5 = top anchor) is published outright in the companion DMQ_scales sheet rather than inferred, so no route was needed for it; and the comparison covers one country deployment (sid 100110) of the 21 the live table pools. Re-runnable as verify_peters_2025_pbc_cond_presence.R (VERDICT: PASS).
